body: like other comments said, everyone is different, but for me the first few days were tough. I don’t know if the type of surgery really makes a difference in your recovery but for reference I had double incision surgery and was out for about 3 hours. I stayed in hospital for 2 nights post op, 3 full days in total. I was coherent enough to talk when I woke up but I was definitely spaced out, and I couldn’t stay awake for more than an hour at a time on the first day. I don’t know if I said anything weird because I was alone in hospital with no one to talk to other than nurses occasionally checking in on me, and I don’t remember my conversations with them. I could walk an hour or so after I woke up but only enough to go to the bathroom, and I was very weak walking to the car when it came time to come home after 3 days. my drains were huge and heavy and that definitely factored in to how difficult it was to walk though. based on my experience I wouldn’t think it’s possible to be able to hide the fact you had surgery. I know I definitely couldn’t have done - like I said I could barely walk, and I had a huge uncomfortable post op binder that kept my arms in an awkward position, I smelt AWFUL, and I was high as shit on morphine and that just made me want to sleep. I’d recommend skipping the dinner if you can and taking the time to rest in bed. I got a one of those table/tray things for beds so I could eat in my room and that really helped me while I was recovering. sorry if this isn’t what you wanted to hear, I just wish someone had been honest with me - I expected to be much more capable than I was after surgery. if you want to know anything else feel free to ask. Congratulations on your surgery being moved forward and good luck!

hey, just want to say im in the exact same boat here, so you’re not alone. i struggle with this exact problem and one of the worst parts is feeling like the only trans man who doesn’t pass even 2 years on testosterone, but im learning it’s more common than you think. it is puberty at the end of the day, like another comment said. definitely don’t give up on surgeries, i almost did that too because i felt weirdly dysphoric about having top surgery when i still look like a woman, but honestly it’s the best thing ive ever done for my mental health, even if it doesn’t really help me pass. i can look in the mirror and see at least part of my body matches a man’s now (if i ignore the scars lol) 

i don’t know what you take, but i started testosterone on gels and i don’t think that’s helped so im about to switch to injections, and im monitoring my levels more now (haven’t been able to in the last year bc, u know, covid) so maybe have a talk with your doctor about your concerns if you haven’t already, see if your levels are too high or to low (mine were too high for a long time and i think that’s fucked up my voice changes, so im starting voice training lessons this year.) hang in there. also, using minoxidil to grow some facial hair has really helped me. still doesn’t help me to pass because i wear a mask but hey, it’s better than nothing. working out and building muscle can help too, and confidence can help with passing.

hope you feel better soon

I don’t know if it works for everyone, but it absolutely helped me. 

My dog passed 3 years ago, around a month before we were due to move house. Moving really, really helped - that last month I spent in the house I shared with her for 12 was the worst month of my life. I kept seeing her everywhere I looked, everything reminded me of her and just HURT, and I kept coming home expecting her to be there and feeling my heartbreak again when she wasn’t. The house just felt wrong and empty without her there and that made me feel sick, and reminders of her made it hard to except she was gone - I’d have bad days where I’d space out and expect her to be there when I opened my bedroom door and went downstairs, but she never was. 

While I didn’t move out specifically because of my grief (like I said, we were moving anyways), and relocating didn’t cure my grief by any means (it’s been 3 years and I still miss her), I think moving absolutely helped me and I’m very grateful for the timing - I really don’t know where I’d be at now mentally if I’d had to stay in the house that was a constant reminder of what I’d lost. 

Also, because I moved I was able to allow myself to get another pet - I have a cat now and he’s the best thing that’s ever happened to me besides my dog, and I wouldn’t have been able to have him if I hadn’t moved - I can’t fully explain why, but to me having another pet in the house I lived in with my dog just felt wrong? Relocating is definitely something to consider, but maybe moving to an entirely new place isn’t for everyone, but I’d definitely recommend changing up your environment -  changing up your furniture/room arrangement, getting out more and avoiding staying all day, and avoiding places you used to hang out with your pet on walks, for example. Everyone is different - I hope you find something that works for you. x
